approach: The root cause is already fixed in code. The budget was checked per invocation, after reading and planning had spent, against a reserve that left out the critic and every later planning round. `reading::budget_reserve` (reading.rs:116) is now the one reserve. It sums the caps only through `Config::planning_usd`, `critic_usd`, `run_usd` and `budget_required` (config.rs:898-935). `Athena::preflight` (reading.rs:490) applies it at six call sites: admission (`first_reading`, reading.rs:1203), retry (reading.rs:1303), dispatch (run/mod.rs:1108), the planner (run/planning.rs:116), the critic (run/planning.rs:336) and the run stage (run/mod.rs:1367). I re-read all six this round. I audited every spend site and found no spend path that starts planning before the reserve is judged. `correct` and the re-read after a configuration change spend only the reader, bounded by `check_budget` (reading.rs:586), and the next `go` judges them at dispatch. So this change adds no production check and no refusal rule. It adds tests that fail when any one preflight is removed or when the reserve drops a cap. The tests are one per entry point, a table over all six caps at all ten stage forms, and two drain tests through `RealSteps`. A syntax-tree scan proves there is no second sum of caps in core. Doc notes and a CHANGELOG entry that states 0% of past accepted readings are newly refused complete the change. Round-3 changes: the scan now parses each file with `syn` and skips only `#[cfg(test)]` items (it never cuts a file), `+=` is a sum, and a planted-source self-test proves it. The scan and CHANGELOG tests moved from reading.rs to a new module at the end of run/tests.rs, so the text that reading.rs source searches key on is untouched. The not-gated tests assert a base reading that is not hard, and the drain tests read the lander's id pairs correctly.

decisions.choice: Add no production check. Keep `Athena::correct` and the re-read after a configuration change (run/mod.rs:1043-1047, then run/pin.rs:149) as they are, with only the reader cap check (reading.rs:586). Record the audit as comments and pin it with two tests (`preflight_correct_is_not_gated_by_admission`, `preflight_reread_is_not_gated_by_admission`).
decisions.reason: Both paths spend at most one reader call and start no planning. The next `go` is judged by the Dispatch preflight (run/mod.rs:1108) before any planner, producer or verifier spend. Admission counts every planning round (config.rs:929-935, 934). In the shipped hard mode (athena.toml [job_plan] mode hard, planner and critic 3.00, max_rounds 5) an unplanned job needs 15.00 at dispatch but 47.00 at Admission, with job_usd 50.00. An Admission check in `correct` or the re-read would refuse corrections that work today. That is a new refusal rule, and its share cannot be measured because records/ is absent from the snapshot.

decisions.choice: Round-3 answer to finding 1. `no_second_sum_of_stage_caps_in_core` parses each core source file with `syn::parse_file` and walks it with a `syn::visit::Visit` visitor. It skips nothing by position: it skips only the subtree of an item carrying `#[cfg(test)]` (a mod, fn, impl, const, static, trait or impl item), and the parser brace-matches that subtree. A `#[cfg(test)] mod name;` declaration has no body and is a no-op, and code after it is scanned. The visitor flags (a) an `ExprBinary` whose operator is `+` or `+=` (`BinOp::Add` or `BinOp::AddAssign`) when either operand mentions one of reader_usd, planner_usd, critic_usd, producer_usd or verifier_usd as an identifier, and (b) a method call named `sum` whose receiver or arguments mention one. A separate structural pass walks the same non-test code and asserts that `fn budget_reserve` is defined once and that every call of `.planning_usd(`, `.run_usd(`, `.critic_usd(` or `.budget_required(` sits inside it. Files named `tests.rs`, `*_tests.rs` or `test_support.rs` are skipped by name, as `code_health::is_measured` does (code_health.rs:195-204). The scan fails if it finds a strict `#[cfg(test)] mod x;` declaration whose name is not `tests` or `*_tests`, so a new test file cannot hide code. A self-test `cap_sum_scanner_flags_planted_sums_and_ignores_test_code` runs the same scanner on string fixtures.
decisions.reason: The earlier text cut (at the first `#[cfg(test)]` line, or at one followed by `mod`) hid production code: lib.rs:154-155 is `#[cfg(test)] mod run_pin_tests;` and production items follow (Quiet at 187, Athena at 229); run/mod.rs:1531-1532 is `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod check_seam {` and production code runs on to 2602. An AST visitor needs no position rule. athena-core already depends on `syn` and `proc-macro2` (athena-core/Cargo.toml:19 and 23; root Cargo.toml:49 and 51 give `span-locations` and `full`, `parsing`, `visit`), and code_health.rs:109 uses the same `Visit` pattern on these files. `+=` is `BinOp::AddAssign` in syn 2, so it is caught by construction.

rejected.option: Cut each file at the first `#[cfg(test)]` followed by `mod`
rejected.why: It hides about 1,070 production lines in run/mod.rs and the lib.rs items after 155.

The note depends only on `resumable_job` and `read_resume` (reading.rs:1308-1310). If it is not printed after the config commit, the producer adjusts the fixture, never `retry`.

risks.risk: The syntax-tree scan could fail on a core file `syn` cannot parse, or flag a legitimate production sum that mentions a cap name.
risks.mitigation: code_health.rs already parses every tracked file with `syn::parse_file`, and my grep of every production mention of the five cap names in core found none inside a `+` or `.sum`. A failure names file:line and the text. If a file is a false positive, the producer adjusts the test's skip rule or its empty allow-list with a stated reason, never production code. The scan covers only the five named cap fields, and the structural pass covers the four Config methods.

risks.risk: A gated statement or expression inside a production fn (for example `#[cfg(test)] { … }` at run/mod.rs:1770) is not skipped by the scan.
risks.mitigation: This only makes the scan stricter, never blind: a cap sum there would be flagged. The scan hides item-level test code only, which is not compiled in production. No such statement mentions a cap name today.
